title: Aspectual RT Set as Higher-Order RT
purpose: Consolidate the insight that distinction, asymmetry, orientation, admissibility, residue, and closure are not independent modules but RT-bearing expressions whose lawful set may itself constitute a higher-order RT expression.

core_claim.statement: A lawful set of RT expressions is itself an aspectual RT expression.
core_claim.reading: The set of RTs is not a mere collection; it is a higher-order process expression when its members preserve lawful distinction, ordering, admissibility, and closure.

aRT.definition: Aspectual or aggregate RT: a higher-order RT whose members are themselves RT expressions.

RT_set.definition: A collection of RT expressions under a shared admissible process context.

candidate_members.RT_closure: RT expression of stable recursive closure
candidate_members.RT_topology: RT expression of projected structural organization

formal_candidate.higher_order: aRT_process := RT({RT_D, RT_asym, RT_orientation, RT_admissibility, RT_residue, RT_closure})

governance_rule.statement: No RT member may be ablated as though it were an independent substance-module without first specifying whether the ablation preserves the higher-order aRT expression.
governance_rule.consequence: Component ablation results are hypothesis-generating only unless an admissible whole-expression substitute is defined.

simulation_reinterpretation.old_question: What happens if orientation/residue/admissibility is removed?
simulation_reinterpretation.new_question: What RT aspect is the metric evaluating, and does the modified run still instantiate a lawful aRT?
simulation_reinterpretation.m3_no_orientation_warning: If orientation removal destroys an RT aspect required for aRT coherence, collapse cannot be interpreted as proof that orientation alone causes closure.
simulation_reinterpretation.m2_no_residue_warning: Weak residue separation may indicate poor residue implementation or metric insensitivity, not residue irrelevance.

required_truth_conditions.TC_ART_001: Each member RT_i must preserve nonzero distinction.
required_truth_conditions.TC_ART_002: The RT_set must have an admissible ordering or coupling relation.
required_truth_conditions.TC_ART_003: The RT_set must produce a higher-order Law-Operator-Truth reading.
required_truth_conditions.TC_ART_004: Removing or altering one RT_i must be evaluated as deformation of the whole aRT, not isolated variable removal.
required_truth_conditions.TC_ART_005: Projection equivalence of two aRT outputs does not imply process identity unless traces also correspond.

open_questions.question: Is every lawful collection of RT expressions an aRT, or only collections with closure?
Does aRT require asymmetric ordering among member RTs?
Can aRT be represented as an array-backed relation among RT expressions?
What is the distinction floor for an RT-set?
Can aRT collapse while member RTs remain locally nonzero?

textbook_targets: Chapter 3: Directed Distinction as Node Formation

promotion_requires: simulation campaign using whole-expression perturbations instead of simple ablations

next_campaign.objective: Replace component ablation tests with lawful aRT deformation tests.
next_campaign.primary_question: Do stable closures persist under admissible aRT deformation better than under component-removal controls?
